taxonomyNote: Animal Diversity Web notes a former subspecies, now Varanus ornatus, is recognised as a separate species.
fieldMarks: Very large lizard: typical adults about 5 ft (up to about 2.4 m) with a neck longer than the narrow head and a laterally compressed, rudder-like tail about 1.5 times body length.
Olive-green to black or brownish with cream or yellow stripes on the jaw and head and rows of yellowish V-shaped stripes from the neck that become bands or spots on the back.
Forked blue-black tongue and long sharp claws; juveniles are black with bold yellow cross-bars and spots.
Nothing native to the U.S. reaches this size with these features (USGS).
behavior: Semi-aquatic, mostly diurnal, basking on rocks and branches and often near water; strong swimmer that can stay under for 12-15 minutes.
Skilled climber; sleeps on branches or submerged in warm weather or in burrows when cooler; lays 12-60 eggs in burrows.
Generalist predator of crabs, crayfish, mollusks, fish, frogs, reptiles, birds, eggs and small mammals.
habitat: In Florida, favoured habitat is along canal systems and water edges, including coastal mangroves and salt marshes; native habitat is woodland, savanna, scrub, swamp and mangrove near water.
range: Native to sub-Saharan Africa and the Nile valley. Non-native in the United States: established in Lee (Cape Coral) and Palm Beach counties, Florida; USGS NAS also records sightings in Georgia, Texas, Arizona, California and Virginia. Not in Canada.
